endorsements.quote: LLMs must be trained on diverse datasets, and the evaluation phase should include a thorough assessment of bias and fairness in predictions, as discussed next.
LLMs must be trained on diverse datasets, and the evaluation phase should include a thorough assessment of bias and fairness in predictions, as discussed next.

To ensure safe deployment, validation of LLMs in healthcare should routinely assess calibration and incorporate correction techniques to align model confidence with real-world reliability [ 25 , 26 ].
Standardised reporting using emerging guidelines such as TRIPOD-LLM [ 38 ] will be crucial for improving transparency, reproducibility, and methodological comparability across studies.
Establishing clear accountability is essential for LLM adoption, and regulatory frameworks must address liability concerns to protect both patients and healthcare professionals.

To build trust and speed up clinical integration, LLMs must incorporate explainability mechanisms that allow transparent evaluation and reduce potential biases, ultimately supporting fair predictions.
Providing clear documentation tailored to different user groups will further support this implementation.

unlisted_practices: Develop hybrid models combining LLMs with traditional survival analysis approaches such as Cox regression to account for censoring and competing risks.
Use federated learning to reduce infrastructure costs and improve data privacy when training LLMs for clinical prediction.
Fine-tune LLMs on the setting in which they are deployed rather than using non-fine-tuned models.
Develop standardised metrics and validation methods for multi-outcome LLM predictions.
Use cross-validation, bootstrapping, or approximating techniques for internal validation of LLMs instead of relying on a data subset.
Use proper data splits between pretraining, fine-tuning and validation of LLMs to prevent overfitting.
Develop tailored, adaptive regulatory frameworks specific to LLMs.
Develop educational programs on LLM healthcare regulations, ethics and law.
Involve interdisciplinary researchers, patient-public involvement, and health professionals in LLM development and co-design.
Form public-private partnerships to share the costs and expertise of LLM infrastructure.
Update GDPR compliance protocols to address LLM-specific requirements.
